$comment: EXP-1490 (eMCP E1, epic VAPP-175, 2026-10-31): WHO SEES WHICH APP TOOL. ONE ENDPOINT, `/api/mcp/apps`, ONE OAUTH FLOW: the consent page picks ONE team, the apps (all, or a list) and Read only | Full, and connects missing upstreams inline (upstream.json). THE GRANT MODEL: `mcp_grants` (one row per user × OAuth client × kind; the unique key becomes (user_id, client_id, kind)) gains `kind` (`grantKinds`: `builtin` = the existing `/api/mcp` grant over teams/boards, every existing row; `apps` = a `/api/mcp/apps` grant), `all_apps` (boolean, default false), `app_ids` (jsonb string[], default []) and `access` (`grantAccess`: `read` | `full`, default `full`). An `apps` grant names exactly one team in `team_ids` (`all_teams` false), no boards, and EITHER `all_apps` OR a non-empty `app_ids` (never both); a `builtin` grant has no apps and access `full` (`grantErrors` → the reasons, `grantCases`; a malformed row grants nothing). `all_apps` covers apps created later; `app_ids` naming a trashed or deleted app simply stops matching it. THE ACCESS RULE (`effectiveAccess`, `accessCases`): levels `none` < `read` < `write`; effective access to an app = the grant (`read` → read, `full` → write) ∩ the member's policy for that app ∩ (per tool) the tool's level. The member's POLICY is the Settings › MCP Access table (member × app, set by owners): no row = the app's DEFAULT (#FEED-242: `apps.default_access` none | read | write, default `write`, set by owners as the table's "Everyone else" row; server-only), except that the app's CREATOR and the team's OWNERS are EXEMPT from the default (no row = `write` for them); an explicit row always wins, for them too (`memberPolicy(row, {default, exempt})`, `policyCases`; no context = default `write`, not exempt). A member whose policy is `none` sees the app nowhere (shapes, tRPC, records, broker, MCP). Owners set the default and members' rows in the Settings table, tRPC `appAccess.setDefault` / `set`, or MCP `exponential_apps_write {op: "access"}`. Access is `none` for an app outside the grant (another team, not listed), a trashed app, a caller who is no longer a member of the grant's team, a grant of kind `builtin` or a malformed grant. A tool is VISIBLE (listed in tools/list) and CALLABLE iff the effective level ≥ its `access` (`visibleCases`): a read token never sees a write tool, and a call to a tool not listed answers MCP's unknown-tool error, never a hint that it exists. Destructive tools never exist (exposes.json). REVOCATION CASCADES: deleting the grant (Settings › MCP Clients, or the member leaving the team) or the OAuth client deletes its access and refresh tokens in the same transaction; trashing an app drops its tools on the next tools/list (the broker sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` to live sessions); removing an upstream server deletes every member's credential for it (the existing `mcp_credentials` cascade) and its bindings answer `upstreamMissing` (upstream.json). #EXP-1720 THE ASSISTANT'S SCOPE (`assistantScope`, `assistantScopeCases`): ONE Assistant per member lives in their hidden personal team (`teams.kind = personal`) and its tree works across their teams. Its teams for a turn = the composer's Teams pick, stored on its conversation root (`sessions.scope_team_ids`; null = every team, `[]` = none) ∩ the teams the member belongs to NOW, in the member's order, deduplicated, always led by the personal team (its own conversation). The gate clamps every request of an Assistant tree to exactly these teams whatever credential carried it (its key is minted `purpose: agent` over the member's teams: a team the member leaves drops out at once); a request naming any other team is refused like a team agent's outside its team. Audit (`mcp_calls.team_id`) = the team of the resolved target.
